According to the 2023 ACR guidelines for ILD, are the following recommended FOR or AGAINST as 1st line treatment for RP-ILD (from Systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases)? 

1. Methotrexate? [...] 
2. Leflunomide? [...] 
3. Azathioprine? [...] 
4. TNFi? [...] 
5. Abatacept? [...] 
6. Tocilizumab? [...] 
7. Nintedanib? [...] 
8. Pirfenidone? [...] 
9. PLEX? [...]

options.explanation:
Methotrexate? AGAINST
Leflunomide? AGAINST
Azathioprine? AGAINST
TNFi? AGAINST
Abatacept? AGAINST
Tocilizumab? AGAINST
Nintedanib? AGAINST
Pirfenidone? AGAINST
PLEX? AGAINST

Essentially, the treatment options for RP-ILD are:
IV steroids, Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, IVIG, MMF, CNIs, or JAKi

***if patient has MDA5 RP-ILD, there is a conditional recommendation for "triple therapy", which is:
IV steroids + 2 of the above options (Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, IVIG, MMF, CNIs, or JAKi)

text:
A 28-year-old female with SLE has been stable on HCQ weight-based for many years. She has been off of prednisone for many years. She has been complaining of chest pain with exertion that is new to her. Her most recent blood work showed Hgb count of 8, but the remainder of her blood work has remained normal. A direct Coombs test is positive. What is your next best step?

A) restart her prednisone but no more than 5mg daily
B) start methotrexate
C) start prednisone in combination with IVIG and/or rituximab
D) start azathioprine in combination with prednisone
E) start prednisone in combination with belimumab

options.text: restart her prednisone but no more than 5mg daily
start prednisone in combination with IVIG and/or rituximab
options.explanation: CORRECT! According to ACR: "Hemolytic Anemia: For symptomatic autoimmune hemolytic anemia (i.e., ischemic manifestations and/or hemodynamic instability) attributed to SLE: We CONDITIONALLY RECOMMEND initial glucocorticoid therapy with addition of IVIG and/or anti-CD20 therapy over the addition of conventional immunosuppressive agents." ***this is the same answer and treatment for symptomatic thrombocytopenia attributed to SLE***

options.text: start azathioprine in combination with prednisone
start prednisone in combination with belimumab

text: A patient has newly diagnosed SLE with concomitant Class IV lupus nephritis. She was started on weight-based HCQ, then induction steroids, followed by MMF in combination with belimumab. She continued to have worsening renal disease — her regimen was switched to MMF in combination with voclosporin. She is continuing to have moderate proteinuria and hematuria on routine labs. What are your next options for treatment, according to ACR?

options.explanation: You have 3 choices, according to ACR: 1) do combination MMF, belimumab, and CNI (ie. voclosporin). 2) add anti-CD20 to current regimen 3) referral for investigational therapy "In people with any LN class with refractory disease (i.e., failed two standard therapy courses), we CONDITIONALLY RECOMMEND treatment escalation to a more intensive regimen, including addition of anti-CD20 agents, OR combination therapy with three non-glucocorticoid immunosuppressives (i.e., MPAA, belimumab and CNI)....OR referral for investigational therapy."

text: Within the 2023 ACR ILD guidelines, which is/are the recommendations classified as 'STRONGLY'?

options.explanation: There is only 1 "STRONG" recommendation, and it is "STRONGLY RECOMMEND AGAINST." "For people with SSc-ILD, we STRONGLY RECOMMEND against glucocorticoids as a first-line ILD treatment."

text: A female patient with rash that develops after prolonged walking/standing/hiking/long plane flights. Some eye dryness. No ulcers, Raynauds, joint pains, fevers, etc. Skin biopsy shows LCV. Negative hepatitis serologies, +RF. What is next test to check?

text: In patients with CVID, what bacterial joint infection is most likely (what organisms)?

text: A 40 year old female with a known history of SLE comes to you for follow up. She has been stable on weight based HCQ. She previously had rashes and arthralgia as her main symptoms, however she has been without those symptoms for the past few years. She has no other known medical problems. Lately however she has been complaining of some SOB and worsening fatigue. She also said her legs have felt a little swollen. Her PCP prescribed furosemide 40mg to take as needed which has helped her swelling. What do you do?
